Using the sources and your own knowledge, discuss the view that the Cultural Revolution demonstrates that Mao’s China was a totalitarian state.
items.answer: The Cultural Revolution shows totalitarian ambitions and power to mobilise, but also the limits of control in practice.
items.markingKey: Indicative content – supporting: Mao cult and mobilisation of millions; purge of Liu Shaoqi and Deng; destruction of culture and Four Olds. Challenging: factional violence escaped control; army needed to restore order; silent resistance in the countryside (Dikötter). Judgement: The Cultural Revolution shows totalitarian ambitions and power to mobilise, but also the limits of control in practice. items.stem: Evaluate the strengths and weaknesses of the argument that historians disagree mainly because of the political context in which they write.
items.answer: Context matters but evidence and method are equally important sources of disagreement.
